conviction_note: A probably clean Q3 (Clean Energy's first full quarter on its accretive Rio Grande charter after 20.5 off-hire days in Q2, plus lower interest cost) roughly offsets the January 1, 2027 UK sanctions cliff on 34.5% of revenue, which the release will restate six weeks before the deadline; with no consensus, no option chain and no sealed history, p_up 53 on an abs move of 5% gives +0.3. The findings sum to +0.4, close to the scaled number because both measurements rest on the same thin lean.
bar: unsourced. No Q3 2026 consensus found: Benzinga and Fox Business show blank or N/A estimates (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DLNG/earnings-forecasts), and Seeking Alpha and Digrin are paywalled. The company gives no earnings guidance. Proxy bar used here: Q2 2026 voyage revenue of $41.2M, adjusted EPU $0.39 and adjusted EBITDA $27.6M (https://finviz.com/news/389607/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-six-months-ended-june-30-2026), and Q3 2025 at revenue $38.9M, adjusted EPU $0.36, adjusted EBITDA $27.6M (https://quartr.com/events/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-dlng-q3-2025_FG0GgqFM). print_vs_bar_pct is revenue against the Q2 run-rate. Every finding is capped small because the bar is unsourced.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 140.0K units with about 2.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (41.9K at 09-15), per curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dlng/short-interest/). Equibles shows an identical 140,249 at 2026-05-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dlng/short-interest), so the figure is not fully reliable. Either way it is a few tenths of a percent of units: not crowded, and no squeeze mechanism. No skew: the baseline option chain is empty (status empty_chain). Tape: spot $2.95 on 2026-11-20, -11.1% over 20 days, -6.65% over 5 days, at the 52-week low and 31% off the high. Turnover is about 56K units a day (about $165K). The slide runs from 3.78 on Oct 1 to 2.95. It includes the Nov 13 ex-date of the $0.05 distribution (3.26 to 3.16) and the Nov 3 sanctions update (3.17 to 3.04 over two sessions), per Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DLNG?range=1y&interval=1d).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is Clean Energy's first full quarter on its new Rio Grande LNG time charter (started 2026-04-30 at a higher rate that management called accretive). Q2 lost 20.5 off-hire days on that vessel between redeliveries and still printed voyage revenue $41.2M, adjusted EPU $0.39 and adjusted EBITDA $27.6M, with net interest costs down 26.9% YoY. Q3 should therefore show revenue around $42-43M and adjusted EPU at or above Q2's $0.39, against Q3 2025's $38.9M and $0.36. There is no consensus to beat, so the comparison is against the trailing quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From Yahoo daily bars, not the baseline, which is empty. Q2 2026 (bmo, 2026-09-08): net income +17% and revenue +6.7% YoY, stock 3.66 to 3.86, +5.5%. Q1 2026 (released 2026-05-29): adjusted net income -13% on lower Arctic Aurora hire and repairs, about -2%. Q4 2025 (released 2026-03-13): revenue and adjusted EBITDA down YoY, about -4% on the day and about -10% over two sessions, though the feed's dates appeared shifted by a day. Quarters with clean revenue have been bought; quarters with a softer revenue line have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: No published estimate exists, so nobody holds a number the full-quarter Rio Grande hire could beat or miss. The stock has fallen 22% since Oct 1 on sanctions headlines, not on operations. If the market had priced an improving quarter, the units would not sit at the 52-week low at roughly 2x annualised adjusted EPU.
findings.independence: The Q4 2025 release (https://finviz.com/news/337229/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-twelve-months-ended-december-31-2025) separately states that the Rio Grande charter is at a higher daily rate and expected to be accretive. It is the same company, a different document. Q2 2026 results also say drydockings fall in 2027-2028, not 2026 (https://quartr.com/events/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-dlng-q2-2026_FG0G6456). Contract coverage is 100% for 2026, so revenue is a utilisation question.

findings.finding: The release will restate the UK sanctions position. Regulations enacted 2026-05-20 bar UK persons from facilitating maritime transport of Russian-origin LNG from 2027-01-01 for the long-term Yamal Trade charters of the Yenisei River and Lena River (to 2033 and 2034; 34.5% of H1 2026 revenue). The company must replace UK-based providers, including insurers, and said on Nov 3 there is 'no assurance that replacement services will be available on comparable terms, or at all'. Losing the charters 'could cause a default under the debt agreements'. The results come six weeks before the deadline: any progress on replacement insurers would be new and positive; a repeat of the Nov 3 wording, or a charterer dispute, would be negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 3 sanctions update (released 16:05 ET) was followed by 3.17 to 3.04 over the next two sessions, about -4%. No earlier print carried a deadline this close.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock is at the 52-week low and fell after the Nov 3 update. What is not priced is the status of insurer replacement, which no public source reports for Dynagas: the search found no named replacement P&I club. If the market had priced a successful switch, the units would have recovered from the 52-week low. If it had priced a charter loss, they would trade well below a 2x multiple, since the two charters are 34.5% of revenue.
findings.independence: Same jurisdictional fact in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/389607/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-six-months-ended-june-30-2026), so the documents are not independent. Lloyd's lobbied for a delay to the UK insurance ban (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/uk/news/marine/lloyds-lobbies-for-delay-as-uks-ban-on-insuring-russian-lng-tankers-approaches-589518.aspx; date not verified). Shares the Nov 3 document with nothing else filed here.

findings.finding: The two other sanctions regimes eased after the Q2 print. On 2026-10-16 an Executive Order waived nearly all of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act's Russia provisions, including those that would have reached Novatek as Yamal LNG's controlling shareholder (Act signed 2026-09-18). The EU's 21st package (adopted 2026-07-23) exempts legacy pre-2022 long-term contracts to at least 2027-07-25, and the company believes the Yamal charters qualify. The UK rule is the remaining live constraint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US waiver week (Oct 16) saw the stock fall from 3.42 to 3.30, so the market did not reward the easing. No print reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and partly priced. It would matter only if the release explicitly states that the US and EU risks have receded and leaves the UK as the sole issue. That would make the risk section read narrower than the Nov 3 notice, which addressed the UK only.
findings.independence: The gCaptain piece of 2026-09-21 names Dynagas as exposed to the Act (https://gcaptain.com/u-s-sanctions-law-puts-russias-arctic-yamal-lng-fleet-in-crosshairs/). High North News reports the EU exemption, 2026-08-04 (https://en.highnorthnews.com/politics/eu-softens-russian-lng-sanctions-allowing-shipping-and-trading-to-continue-beyond-2027/1115356). This is a proxy at company level: the company has confirmed only the EU part.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-12, after the quarter, the partnership redeemed 2,000,000 of its 3,000,000 9.00% Series A preferred units at $25, a $50M cash outlay, from 'available liquidity'. Cash was $59.5M at 2026-06-30. The release will show the Sept 30 cash and, as a subsequent event, a much thinner balance going into the Jan 1 UK deadline. That deadline is one the company itself links to possible debt default. What the money buys: retiring 9% paper saves about $4.5M a year of preferred distributions, roughly $0.12 a common unit a year, which is accretive. What it costs is a liquidity cushion ahead of a sanctions cliff.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day (2026-10-09) closed 3.70 to 3.60, -2.7%, and the slide continued afterwards. No print history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The redemption itself is priced, announced Oct 9. The pro-forma liquidity number is not public: no figure after June 30 exists. If the market had seen a comfortable residual cash figure, it would not have kept selling into the Nov 3 sanctions notice.
findings.independence: The Q2 release gives the June 30 cash of $59.5M and sale-leaseback debt of about $256.6M (https://finviz.com/news/389607/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-reports-results-for-the-three-and-six-months-ended-june-30-2026). Stocktitan lists the Oct 9 redemption notice (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/DLNG/). The two sources reinforce each other; they are not independent of the redemption fact.

outside_window.finding: The $10M common unit repurchase program expires 2026-11-24. Last year's renewal was announced 2025-12-10, after the prior program expired 2025-11-21, so a renewal most likely lands after the exit window.
UK maritime services ban on Russian LNG takes effect for the Yamal charters on 2027-01-01. Whether the charters survive (insurer replacement, charterer stance) resolves then.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. A mildly positive operational lean cuts against a -11% 20-day run-up and a 52-week-low tape, which reflect the sanctions cliff that the release will restate, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the preferred redemption buys (it retires 9% paper, about $0.12 a common unit a year, accretive) against the liquidity cost ahead of the cliff; the redemption shrank from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission): the US waiver and EU exemption are confirmed by the company only for the EU part; shrank from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): every finding was already capped small; nothing further changed.
Lesson 1 (verified fact versus reaction): this name bought the clean Q2 (+5.5%) and sold the softer Q1 and Q4, so the reported-quarter finding stays at +1.0.
